However, the municipalities will be dependent upon increased tax revenues derived from secondary business development, new housing and other sources which will undoubtedly provide significant additional municipal tax. However, these are not likely to meet all additional revenue requirements. The Montana Coal Severance Tax is presently generating significant new revenues some of which may become available to the munincipalities. If special financial assistance is not available elsewhere there will be serious and unavoidable lag between the time that the additional services are required and the revenues become available.
Transportation
Existing county and other public roads within the mine areas are to be relocated as necessary and maintained in a usable condition and then replaced in equal or better condition at the chosen location. Railroad and road plans are required to contain provisions for protecting the environment to the greatest extent possible. For, example, normal surface water flow and drainage should be uninterrupted by construction of bridges or placements of culverts. Federal Highway Department standards govern design of many features, signals, and underpasses at crossings. The plans must specify how fertilization and reseeding will be used to repair any disturbed natural vegetation or barren areas.
